Powdery mildew.description: A fungal disease that appears as a white, powdery coating on leaves, stems, and sometimes flowers.
Powdery mildew.treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves. Apply a sulfur-based fungicide or a horticultural oil according to label directions.
Powdery mildew.prevention: Improve airflow (avoid overcrowding), reduce leaf wetness, and water at the base. Use resistant varieties when available.

Downy mildew.description: A fungal-like disease causing yellow patches on the upper leaf surface and gray-purple growth underneath (often in humid conditions).
Downy mildew.treatment: Remove infected foliage immediately. Use a recommended downy-mildew fungicide (e.g., copper-based or targeted products) and repeat as per label.
Downy mildew.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, space plants for airflow, and keep the canopy dry.

Late blight.description: A destructive disease (common in potatoes and tomatoes) with dark, water-soaked lesions that can spread rapidly in cool, wet weather.
Late blight.treatment: Remove infected plants/foliage. Use a labeled late-blight fungicide and follow a preventive schedule when conditions are favorable.
Late blight.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid planting too densely, sanitize tools, and water early so leaves dry quickly.

Leaf spot.description: A group of diseases that create brown/black spots on leaves and may cause premature leaf drop.
Leaf spot.treatment: Prune infected leaves and destroy plant debris. Apply a suitable fungicide if spots are spreading.
Leaf spot.prevention: Water at the soil level, keep foliage dry, and avoid working in wet conditions.

Root rot.description: Often caused by excess moisture and poor drainage; roots become brown/soft and plants wilt or yellow even with adequate watering.
Root rot.treatment: Improve drainage immediately. Remove severely affected plants. Treat soil/containers with appropriate biological or fungicidal products where available.
Root rot.prevention: Use well-draining soil, avoid overwatering, and ensure pots have drainage holes.

Rust.description: A fungal disease producing orange/brown pustules (rust-colored spots) on leaves and stems.
Rust.treatment: Remove infected leaves. Apply a labeled rust fungicide and repeat as directed.
Rust.prevention: Increase airflow, avoid overhead irrigation, and remove volunteer host plants nearby.

Anthracnose.description: A fungal disease that causes dark, sunken spots on leaves and stems; lesions can expand and coalesce.
Anthracnose.treatment: Remove infected parts. Apply a labeled anthracnose fungicide if needed and keep repeating per label intervals.
Anthracnose.prevention: Keep foliage dry, avoid splashing water, and practice crop rotation.

Strawberry with Leaf Scorch.description: Leaf scorch in strawberry typically appears as reddish-purple spots that can merge into dry, scorched-looking leaf margins, reducing plant vigor and yield.
Strawberry with Leaf Scorch.treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves and improve airflow. Apply a labeled fungicide for strawberry leaf diseases (for example captan or copper-based products), following label rates and intervals.
Strawberry with Leaf Scorch.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, reduce leaf wetness duration, remove old infected debris, and maintain spacing for good ventilation.

Cedar Apple Rust.description: A fungal rust disease causing bright yellow-orange leaf spots, often affecting apple leaves and reducing photosynthetic capacity.
Cedar Apple Rust.treatment: Prune and remove nearby alternate hosts where possible and apply a labeled rust fungicide during susceptible growth stages.
Cedar Apple Rust.prevention: Use preventive spray programs in high-risk seasons, improve canopy airflow, and remove infected debris.
